I am 26 with Bipolar I as well. Lately, I've been having some anxieties around the fact that I'm 26 and have done less toward my independent life than many 20 year olds. I've lived on my own a couple times, and gone to college a bit. I can just never keep at anything for more than six or eight months. Right now I'm living with my dad, working a bit, and paying off bills I still have from a manic episode four years ago when I went off my medication. I've never been in any formal care, but my doctor wanted me to when I admitted to cutting and that I wished I would somehow get killed (but that I was not suicidal.) I can be charming and annoyingly convincing. It seems like the times when I want or need help the most are the times when I end up convincing even the most skeptical people that everything is fine.

My biggest internal struggle right now is about work. I've always had a really hard time keeping jobs because I slowly start to hate myself more and more until basically every day I'm cutting myself or wishing desperately to not be alive anymore. I get to the point where I just don't care about my job and intentionally don't think about the consequences of losing it. Right now I've been filling in at a relaxed-environment delivery place. They want to hire me but it makes me really nervous. I've been working on getting my health care straightened out and I'm hoping to get into more active mental health treatment, like counselling. Unfortunately I have some pretty serious anxiety problems and it's hard for me to get the help.

I also struggle with weight, but it's not because of meds, mostly just depression, especially in combination with insomnia. I stay healthy and active, but it's quicker to consume calories than burn them.

I'm glad you are able to work. I can go for a while, but it starts dragging my down slowly and steadily until I can't function any more. Hopefully joining this community is helpful for you. It's a small community still, though. I try to check it every few days.

Great to hear from you. Are we twins? I'm 26 and live with my dad. It feels like I only stay interested in something for 6-8 months. I was able to finish at community college though (I had been planning to teach English abroad before my breakup and needed a 2-yr degree) so that kept me focused. It seems like meds have filled the void that my ex left. I feel pretty normal, although it's the weekend now and I really have no social life or any plans at all. At least it feels normal to be bored. My therapist told me that I don't need to try and sweep the feelings that I'm having under the rug and what I'm going through is pretty normal. Went to a couple job interviews last week (lifeguarding is boring, and more suited to a 16 year old than a 26 year old) and hoping I hear some good news from USPS on Tuesday.

I can relate to the feelings of anxiety and missing out. An acquaintance of mine just closed on a house and is getting married -- she's only 21. Sometimes when I'm manic it feels like I can be popular and make friends. But then with the depression, it all just sort of fades away. I think a lot of friendships are formed on shared experiences and I really haven't had the normal life experiences most others my age have had. I'd love to do peer support for inpatient if only it paid better.

Anyways, thanks for the warm welcome!

P.S. I can relate to wanting to be dead without being suicidal :) Sorry to hear that you cut yourself though, must be rough.

Generally I don't intent to sweep my feelings under the rug, it just kinda happens. It bothers me a lot that I have such a hard time not putting up a front, because then when I fail at meeting expectations people think it reflects my character and not my depression.

Thankfully, my group of friends is the same one from middle school. They predate most of the severe bipolar stuff. Still, though, it seems like when I want to get out of the house the most they are unavailable. I would miss out on a lot of things due to not having money, too.

Cutting is a weird thing. It never made sense to me, and it still doesn't. Fortunately, it hasn't been a problem lately. I don't know if it was a reaction to the stress or the depression, but I'd rather not start down that path again, obviously, so I've been really cautious about stress.
